flashcard_questions.a: The belief in life after death, beginning at the moment a person dies.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Barzakh in Islamic belief?
flashcard_questions.a: The waiting stage between death and the Day of Judgement, spent conscious in the grave.
The angel who will blow the trumpet to announce the Day of Judgement.

flashcard_questions.q: Which angel records a Muslim’s good deeds?
flashcard_questions.a: Raqib, who sits on the right shoulder.

flashcard_questions.q: Which angel records a Muslim’s bad deeds?
flashcard_questions.a: Atid, who sits on the left shoulder.
Paradise — an eternal garden and final home for the faithful and righteous.
Hell — a place of fire and torment for those who reject Allah.
The sin of worshipping anything other than Allah — the only sin Allah will not forgive.

flashcard_questions.q: How many gates does Islamic teaching say Jannah has?
How many levels does Islamic teaching say Jahannam has?
What do Muslims believe they cross to arrive at Jannah?
Which hand receiving the book of deeds means a person enters paradise?
What happens when Israfil blows the trumpet a second time?
flashcard_questions.a: Everyone who has ever lived is raised from the dead with a new body.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Qur’an verse promises that believers who do good dwell in Paradise forever?
How does belief in Akhirah affect daily Muslim life?
flashcard_questions.a: Muslims become more God-conscious, knowing angels record every action for judgement.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term→definition (Akhirah, Barzakh, Jannah, Jahannam, shirk, Israfil), 2 angel→role (Raqib, Atid), 3 numerical/detail facts (eight gates, seven levels, As-Sirat Bridge), 1 belief→source (Qur’an 2:82), 1 practice→meaning (right hand), 2 cause→effect (second trumpet, taqwa). Dropped the literal translation of barzakh to avoid two cards on the same term.
